title: Rosalind and the Clock
premise: In 1919, in a river town cut off each winter when its bridge closes, nurse Xanthe Iversen keeps a secret ledger of soldiers whose deaths officers erased from official records. When the bridge shuts for the season, a wounded stranger arrives carrying proof that Colonel Aldous Vane — the town's benefactor and Xanthe's old commanding officer — falsified casualty reports to protect his inheritance of a family estate. The stranger is Rosalind Vane, the colonel's disinherited daughter, and Xanthe once promised her dying brother he would see justice done. Trapped together by ice, snow, and the colonel's men, Xanthe must choose between the silences that have kept him safe for twenty years and the truth in his ledger. In the spring thaw, as the bridge reopens, Xanthe testifies before a civilian tribunal at terrible personal cost; the colonel falls, Rosalind inherits nothing but the truth, and she and Xanthe leave together across the bridge, carrying the ledger to the families of the forgotten dead.
about_author: Theo Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military hospital records from the Great War. He writes historical fiction about the people history filed under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Xanthe Iversen, now a town nurse, hides his wartime ledger of omitted names beneath his surgery floorboards. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet dread — twenty years of careful silence about to be tested.

chapters.title: Last Cart Across
chapters.summary: The town prepares for the bridge closing; Xanthe treats the last travelers and notes the garrison doubling under Colonel Vane's command. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: claustrophobia as the river becomes a wall.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Surgery Door
chapters.summary: On the final night, a half-frozen woman collapses at Xanthe's door with a bullet wound — Rosalind Vane, presumed dead by her own family. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: shock and recognition of an old promise coming due.

chapters.title: What Her Brother Made Me Swear
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present: Xanthe recalls promising dying Edmund Vane he would expose the falsified reports. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a wound reopened.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Evidence
chapters.summary: Rosalind reveals documents proving her father altered casualty ledgers to claim his brother's estate. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: cold fury sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Dinner Invitation
chapters.summary: Vane summons Xanthe to the garrison house, probing gently about strangers on the road. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the terror of polite menace.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: The bridge officially closes; the town settles into winter isolation, and Vane posts men at the ferry crossing. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the trap tightening.

chapters.title: An Old Nurse's Memory
chapters.summary: Elderly matron Agnes Hale recognizes Rosalind and, instead of betraying her, offers the attic of the disused fever ward as refuge. POV: Agnes. Emotional beat: unexpected solidarity across generations.

chapters.title: The First Search
chapters.summary: Soldiers search the surgery while Xanthe stalls them over tea; the ledger survives by inches. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: adrenaline curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: What Power Buys in a Small Town
chapters.summary: Rosalind observes how Vane's charity has bought every merchant's loyalty and every constable's blindness. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: disillusionment — justice has no purchase here.

chapters.title: The Copyist
chapters.summary: Xanthe begins copying the ledger, entrusting pages to Agnes and the schoolteacher, building a web of witnesses. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: fragile hope through shared risk.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ferry House
chapters.summary: The schoolteacher's nervousness betrays them; a courier is caught with ledger pages and names Xanthe under questioning. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: dread — the noose draws closed.

chapters.title: House Arrest
chapters.summary: Vane places Xanthe under genteel confinement in the garrison house, offering pardon for silence. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: temptation — twenty years of safety offered back like a bribe.

chapters.title: Father and Daughter
chapters.summary: Vane confronts Rosalind privately, revealing he knew she lived all along and offers her the estate if she recants. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging versus integrity.

chapters.title: Agnes's Gambit
chapters.summary: Agnes fakes a typhoid scare to evacuate the fever ward, smuggling Rosalind out amid the panic. POV: Agnes. Emotional beat: defiant courage from the least expected quarter.

chapters.title: The Ice Road
chapters.summary: Rosalind crosses the frozen river toward the magistrate in the county seat, pursued across the ice by Vane's men. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: desperate flight, cracking ice mirroring cracking loyalties.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Vane burns Xanthe's original ledger before him — but Xanthe reveals the copies are already distributed. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: ashes and triumph entwined.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Ledger pages circulate through the town; merchants, constables, and soldiers must each choose sides as the thaw begins. POV: multiple brief voices via Xanthe's observation. Emotional beat: a community waking from complicity.

chapters.title: Confrontation on the Bridge
chapters.summary: As the ice breaks, Vane tries to flee with the estate deeds; Rosalind and Xanthe block the bridge, and the townsfolk stand behind them. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: climax — power meeting the people it corrupted.

chapters.title: The Tribunal in the Schoolhouse
chapters.summary: A civilian tribunal convenes; Xanthe testifies, naming every omitted soldier aloud. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: catharsis — silence finally broken, name by name.

chapters.title: Verdict and Cost
chapters.summary: Vane is stripped of rank and estate; Rosalind refuses the tainted inheritance, endowing it to the soldiers' families. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory — justice without restoration.

chapters.title: Crossing in Spring
chapters.summary: The bridge reopens; Xanthe and Rosalind walk out together carrying copies of the ledger to deliver to the families of the forgotten dead. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: release — the promise kept, the silence ended.
